# Team Asset Tracker — Data Models

## Overview

The database is managed by **Convex**, which uses a document-based (NoSQL) data model defined in `src/convex/schema.ts`. Unlike SQL databases, Convex stores data as JSON-like documents in tables.

## Current Schema

The current schema includes authentication tables auto-generated by `@convex-dev/auth`. The asset-tracking tables below represent the planned data model.

### Auth Tables (Auto-generated)

These are created by `authTables` in `src/convex/schema.ts`:

| Table              | Purpose                                    |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `users`            | User accounts (name, email, image, etc.)   |
| `authAccounts`     | Auth provider links (password, OAuth, etc.)|
| `authSessions`     | Active login sessions                       |
| `authRefreshTokens`| Token refresh management                    |
| `authVerificationCodes` | Email verification codes              |
| `authVerifiers`    | Verification state                          |
| `authRateLimits`   | Rate limiting for auth attempts             |

### Planned Asset Tables

These tables should be created to implement the asset tracking features:

```typescript
// src/convex/schema.ts — planned additions

// Assets table — tracks hardware and software
assets: defineTable({
  name: v.string(),              // "MacBook Pro 16"
  type: v.union(                 // Hardware or software
    v.literal("hardware"),
    v.literal("software")
  ),
  category: v.string(),          // "laptop", "monitor", "license"
  serialNumber: v.optional(v.string()),
  purchaseDate: v.optional(v.string()),
  status: v.union(               // Current assignment status
    v.literal("available"),
    v.literal("assigned"),
    v.literal("maintenance"),
    v.literal("retired")
  ),
  assignedTo: v.optional(v.id("users")),  // ★ Foreign key to users
  receiptFileId: v.optional(v.id("_storage")), // ★ Convex file storage ref
  photoFileId: v.optional(v.id("_storage")),
  notes: v.optional(v.string()),
})
  .index("by_status", ["status"])
  .index("by_assignedTo", ["assignedTo"])
  .index("by_type", ["type"]),

// Employees table (extends users with company info)
employees: defineTable({
  userId: v.id("users"),          // ★ Foreign key to users table
  department: v.string(),         // "Engineering", "Marketing"
  role: v.union(                  // Determines UI access
    v.literal("admin"),
    v.literal("employee")
  ),
  startDate: v.optional(v.string()),
})
  .index("by_userId", ["userId"])
  .index("by_department", ["department"]),
```

```
│ email        │       │ department   │       │              │
│ image        │       │ role         │       │              │
└──────┬───────┘       └──────────────┘       └──────┬───────┘

       │                               photoFileId    │
       ▼                                              │
┌──────────────┐                                      │
│   assets     │◄─────────────────────────────────────┘
│              │
│ _id          │
│ name         │
│ type         │
│ status       │
│ assignedTo ──┼──► users._id
│ receiptFileId┼──► _storage._id
│ photoFileId  ┼──► _storage._id
└──────────────┘
```

## Key Concepts for Interns

### Foreign Keys in Convex

Unlike SQL, Convex uses `v.id("tableName")` to create typed references:

```typescript
// This field can ONLY hold a valid users table ID
assignedTo: v.id("users")
```

### Indexes

Indexes speed up queries that filter by specific fields:

```typescript
// Without index: Convex scans every document
// With index: Convex jumps directly to matching documents
.index("by_status", ["status"])
```

### File Storage References

Convex has built-in file storage. Files are referenced by `v.id("_storage")`:

```typescript
receiptFileId: v.id("_storage")  // Points to an uploaded file
```

To upload: use `generateUploadUrl()` mutation, then store the returned ID.
